en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 9.15.
Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika (The Subsequent Pair: The Triplet of the Wholesome)
Dependent on unwholesome states not to be abandoned by vision … dependent on unwholesome states not to be abandoned by non-vision … (Abbreviated.
Under the root condition there are five; under the object condition, two … under the result condition, one … under the non-disappearance condition, five.
Dependent on unwholesome states not to be abandoned by cultivation … dependent on unwholesome states not to be abandoned by non-cultivation … (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause condition, there are five; in object condition, two … pe … in ripening condition, one … pe … in non-disappearance condition, five.

Dependent on a non-virtuous state whose root is not to be abandoned by insight … pe … dependent on a non-virtuous state whose root is not to be abandoned by non-insight … pe … dependent on a non-virtuous state whose root is not to be abandoned by cultivation … pe … [and so forth].
... pe ... dependent on an unwholesome state with roots to be abandoned by insight cultivation (*nanabhāvanāya pahātabbahetuka*) ... (Abbreviated.

Nine in the case of root-cause (*hetu*), six in the case of object-condition (*ārammaṇa*), five in the case of predominance (*adhipati*) ... pe ... one in the case of result (*vipāka*) ... pe ... nine in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*).

Dependent on a state that is neither with initial application nor wholesome (*nasavitakka-nakusala*) ... pe ... dependent on a state that is neither without initial application nor wholesome (*naavitakka-nakusala*) ... pe ...
... pe ... dependent on a non-vitakka-non-vicāra unwholesome state ... pe ... dependent on a non-avicāra unwholesome state ...
pe ... dependent on a non-pīti unwholesome state ... pe ... dependent on a non-appīti unwholesome state ... pe ...
dependent on a non-pīti-sahagata unwholesome state ... pe ... dependent on a non-na-pīti-sahagata unwholesome state ... pe ...

Dependent on [a state] … dependent on a state that is neither accompanied by pleasure nor wholesome … dependent on a state that is neither accompanied by non-pleasure nor wholesome … dependent on a state that is neither accompanied by equanimity nor wholesome … dependent on a state that is neither accompanied by non-equanimity nor wholesome … (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition, there are nine; ... pe ... with respect to the prenascence and repetition conditions, there are six;

... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition, there are nine. Dependent on a state that is neither of the sense-sphere nor wholesome, ... pe ... dependent on a state that is neither of the sense-sphere nor wholesome, ... pe ...
dependent on a state that is neither of the fine-material sphere nor wholesome, ... pe ... dependent on a state that is neither of the immaterial sphere nor wholesome, ... pe ... [and so forth].
Dependent on ... (Abbreviated.

Nine by way of root, four by way of object, five by way of predominance ... pe ... six by way of mutuality ... pe ... two by way of prenascence and repetition ... pe ... nine by way of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is neither fine-material-sphere nor wholesome ... pe ... dependent on a state that is neither non-fine-material-sphere nor wholesome ... (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are five; in the object condition, two ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.
Dependent on a state that is neither included nor wholesome ... pe ... dependent on a state that is neither included nor wholesome ... (Abbreviated. In the case of the root condition, there are five;
in the object condition, two ... pe ... in the repetition condition, one ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, five.

Dependent on a state that is neither leading out nor wholesome … dependent on a state that is neither leading out nor wholesome … dependent on a state that is not fixed and not wholesome … dependent on a state that is not fixed and not wholesome … (Abbreviated.
Under root: five; under object: two … under result: one … under non-disappearance: five.
Dependent on a state that is neither supreme nor unwholesome … pe … dependent on a state that is neither supreme nor unwholesome … (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are five; under object condition there are two … pe … under repetition condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are five.
Dependent on a state that is neither subject to cankers nor unwholesome, a state that is neither subject to cankers nor unwholesome arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-passion-nor-non-virtuous, a state that is neither-passion-nor-non-virtuous arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-passion-nor-non-virtuous, a state that is neither-refuge-nor-non-virtuous arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-passion-nor-non-virtuous, states that are both neither-refuge-nor-non-virtuous and neither-passion-nor-non-virtuous arise...
They arise by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is neither-secure-nor-unwholesome and neither-secure-nor-unwholesome, a state that is neither-secure-nor-unwholesome arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of root [condition] there are five;
in the case of object (*ārammaṇa*) there are two ... pe ... in the case of result (*vipāka*) there is one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance (*avigata*) there are five.
Dependent on a non-refuge and unwholesome state, a non-refuge and unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
One [condition] under root; (one in every case.
Dependent on a non-refuge and indeterminate state, a non-refuge and indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-ensnaring-nor-indeterminate, there arises a state that is neither-ensnaring-nor-indeterminate by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are two;
under object-condition there are two ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are two.
(The same applies in the section on conascence and in the section on inquiry; the full detail is given everywhere.)
